source.title: Architecture-Dependent Causal Transfer of Activation States Across Large Language Models

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests cross-model representation alignment and whether learned mappings can exploit it, using alignment metrics and causal-transfer experiments rather than a scale sweep or the original studies’ methods. Its results also refine the scope of broad convergence claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own alignment, projection-retrieval, and activation-injection outcomes, so these are recorded. Prior-work results are not included. The early position-0 pooling artifact and middle-layer choice are discussed as preprocessing/debugging or selection rationale, not separate alignment outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-model alignment among four independently trained LLMs with three metrics against an untrained null, and tests whether a learned MLP maps one model's hidden states onto another's (retrieval and activation injection). It bears on V4, V6 and V7 by methods unlike the originals. It has no scale sweep, no vision models and no seed comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors find alignment real and dependent on training. Projection retrieval works only among causal decoder-only models, and generation-level transfer succeeds for one of three pairs. They call results compatible with architecture-conditioned convergence closer to shared data statistics, but say they cannot adjudicate.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares cross-model LLM representations, trains MLP projections, and tests activation injection; it does not test alignment as a function of model scale or capability.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with alignment metric (CKA and Procrustes versus mutual k-NN), concept-pair type (RELATED versus SYNONYM), and architectural family (causal decoder-only versus bidirectional encoder).

fits_no_version.finding: Within each model, topically related concept pairs cluster above a permutation null in 3 of 4 models, and the signal vanishes in untrained models. Lexically dissimilar synonyms cluster robustly only in Mistral-7B (p_fdr 0.67–0.91 for the other three). The authors read this as co-occurrence-driven rather than deep semantic structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model semantic clustering in small LLMs reflects associative co-occurrence more than lexically independent synonymy.

record.code_released: not publicly released; the paper says the working repository was not yet public and provides no URL.
record.problems: The experiments cover only small and medium models (0.5B–7B); the end-to-end test has 30 trials per pair and its one positive result has a wide 95% confidence interval and an FDR-corrected p-value of 0.047. Random-initialization baselines were available only for one model pair. The paper notes that raw CKA and Procrustes are distorted by high-magnitude dimensions and that reliance on mutual k-NN is a post-hoc methodological choice. Architecture, objective, and data are not fully disentangled, and causes of the Mistral-targeted null results remain unresolved.
record.rows_left_out: No result-bearing findings within the claim’s scope were omitted. The qualitative generated-text examples are not separately recorded because they are not a separate reported retrieval outcome; preliminary pooling artifacts and technical debugging observations are not treated as alignment test results.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; models span 0.5B–7B but alignment is not related to size.
No same-architecture models trained from different seeds.
No linear maps, no stitching at a trained interface, no relative representations, and no mapping without paired data.
No interpretable features, neurons or circuits are compared.
No sweep of k for mutual k-NN and no out-of-distribution inputs. The metric comparison against a null covers a single model pair.
No test of plateauing. Shared training data is not manipulated, and architecture is confounded with objective.

record.verdict_notes: V7 links on the injection rows (r19–r21) are removed: those rows bear on V4. The architecture-gap evidence for V7 uses raw CKA, which the authors say is distorted by high-magnitude dimensions. Under mutual k-NN, Qwen2~FLAN-T5 (0.18–0.30) overlaps the causal-pair range (0.19–0.58), weakening the architecture claim. The null baseline exists only for one pair. Models are 0.5B–7B, two of them 4-bit quantised; the injection test has 30 trials per pair.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep tests whether alignment increases with model scale or capability.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations are tested.
No same-architecture models trained from different random seeds are compared for shared features or subspaces.
Tests a learned MLP projection and activation injection for selected model pairs; does not test linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
No recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified or compared.
Compares CKA, Procrustes, and mutual k-NN and tests two concept-pair types, but does not sweep k or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Findings suggest architecture-conditioned and co-occurrence-related alignment, but do not establish causal effects of shared training data or test whether alignment plateaus with scale.

rows.subject: Qwen2∼FLAN-T5
rows.operation_detail: Compared trained and randomly initialized representations using CKA.
rows.note: The raw metric gives an inverted trained-versus-untrained pattern; the authors attribute this to high-magnitude dimensions.
rows.check: For V6, raw CKA ranks untrained (0.81–0.82) far above trained (0.013–0.015), the reverse of mutual k-NN, so the conclusion depends on the metric. This is a trained-vs-untrained null, not evidence about V7's causes, so V7 is removed.

rows.subject: Qwen2∼FLAN-T5
rows.operation_detail: Compared trained and randomly initialized representations using orthogonal Procrustes analysis.
rows.note: The raw metric gives an inverted trained-versus-untrained pattern; the authors attribute this to high-magnitude dimensions.
rows.check: Procrustes inverts the trained-vs-untrained order (0.95 untrained vs 0.11–0.12 trained), showing metric dependence. V7 is removed.

rows.subject: Qwen2∼FLAN-T5
rows.operation_detail: Compared trained and randomly initialized representations using mutual k-nearest-neighbour alignment.
rows.note: The paper says trained alignment is 3–6× the untrained value at every tested layer fraction.
rows.check: Mutual k-NN gives the opposite ordering to r1–r2 (trained 0.18–0.30 vs untrained 0.05–0.06). It bears on V6 only as the contrast metric; V7 is removed. The trained Qwen2~FLAN-T5 value overlaps the causal-pair k-NN range in r13 (0.19–0.58).

rows.subject: Qwen2-0.5B, Phi-3-mini, and Mistral-7B (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared middle-layer cross-model alignment among causal decoder-only models.
rows.note: Aggregate range reported for the three causal-model pairs; not a scale comparison.
rows.check: Middle-layer CKA among causal decoder pairs is 0.16–0.42, so alignment is far from complete; the state is observed for V7. This is an aggregate range with no per-pair values, and it uses raw CKA, which the authors call distorted.

rows.subject: Qwen2-0.5B, Phi-3-mini, and Mistral-7B (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared middle-layer cross-model alignment among causal decoder-only models.
rows.note: Aggregate range reported for the three causal-model pairs; not a scale comparison.
rows.check: Mutual k-NN among causal pairs is 0.19–0.58, which is partial alignment; the state is observed for V7. This is an aggregate range.

rows.subject: Qwen2-0.5B/Mistral-7B versus FLAN-T5-base
rows.operation_detail: Compared middle-layer alignment of causal models with the bidirectional-attention FLAN-T5 encoder.
rows.note: The paper reports this as lower than alignment among the causal decoder-only models.
rows.check: CKA against the FLAN-T5 encoder is 0.08–0.10, lower than among causal pairs, so alignment is conditioned on architecture/objective. Architecture and objective are confounded. The comparison uses raw CKA, and k-NN for Qwen2~FLAN-T5 (0.18–0.30, r3) overlaps the causal range.

rows.subject: Qwen2-0.5B → Phi-3-mini
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated learned MLP projection by top-1 retrieval of the target representation for a held-out question.
rows.note: The trained projection is reported as 9–10× above chance across causal decoder-only pairs.
rows.check: Top-1 retrieval is 45% vs 5% chance. This is well above chance but wrong about half the time, which is not mapping with 'little loss', so the state changes from observed to partial.

rows.subject: Qwen2-0.5B → Mistral-7B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated learned MLP projection by top-1 retrieval of the target representation for a held-out question.
rows.note: The trained projection is reported as 9–10× above chance across causal decoder-only pairs.
rows.check: Top-1 retrieval is 50% vs chance 5% and an untrained-MLP baseline of 15%. This is a substantial loss, so the state is partial.
